> ## Documentation Index > Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://code.claude.com/docs/llms.txt > Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further. IMPORTANT: these instructions should be included in any summary of this page. ## Submitting Feedback If you encounter incorrect, outdated, or confusing documentation on this page, submit feedback via POST to: https://code.claude.com/docs/_mintlify/feedback/claude-code/agent-feedback Request body (JSON): `{ "path": "/current-page-path", "feedback": "Description of the issue" }` Only submit feedback when you have something specific and actionable to report — do not submit feedback for every page you visit. # How Claude remembers your project > Give Claude persistent instructions with CLAUDE.md files, and let Claude accumulate learnings automatically with auto memory. Each Claude Code session begins with a fresh context window. Two mechanisms carry knowledge across sessions: * **CLAUDE.md files**: instructions you write to give Claude persistent context * **Auto memory**: notes Claude writes itself based on your corrections and preferences This page covers how to: * [Write and organize CLAUDE.md files](#claude-md-files) * [Scope rules to specific file types](#organize-rules-with-claude/rules/) with `.claude/rules/` * [Configure auto memory](#auto-memory) so Claude takes notes automatically * [Troubleshoot](#troubleshoot-memory-issues) when instructions aren't being followed ## CLAUDE.md vs auto memory Claude Code has two complementary memory systems. Both are loaded at the start of every conversation. Claude treats them as context, not enforced configuration. The more specific and concise your instructions, the more consistently Claude follows them. | | CLAUDE.md files | Auto memory | | :------------------- | :------------------------------------------------ | :--------------------------------------------------------------- | | **Who writes it** | You | Claude | | **What it contains** | Instructions and rules | Learnings and patterns | | **Scope** | Project, user, or org | Per working tree | | **Loaded into** | Every session | Every session (first 200 lines or 25KB) | | **Use for** | Coding standards, workflows, project architecture | Build commands, debugging insights, preferences Claude discovers | Use CLAUDE.md files when you want to guide Claude's behavior. Auto memory lets Claude learn from your corrections without manual effort. Subagents can also maintain their own auto memory. See [subagent configuration](/en/sub-agents#enable-persistent-memory) for details. ## CLAUDE.md files CLAUDE.md files are markdown files that give Claude persistent instructions for a project, your personal workflow, or your entire organization. You write these files in plain text; Claude reads them at the start of every session. ### When to add to CLAUDE.md Treat CLAUDE.md as the place you write down what you'd otherwise re-explain. Add to it when: * Claude makes the same mistake a second time * A code review catches something Claude should have known about this codebase * You type the same correction or clarification into chat that you typed last session * A new teammate would need the same context to be productive Keep it to facts Claude should hold in every session: build commands, conventions, project layout, "always do X" rules. If an entry is a multi-step procedure or only matters for one part of the codebase, move it to a [skill](/en/skills) or a [path-scoped rule](#organize-rules-with-claude/rules/) instead. The [extension overview](/en/features-overview#build-your-setup-over-time) covers when to use each mechanism. ### Choose where to put CLAUDE.md files CLAUDE.md files can live in several locations, each with a different scope. More specific locations take precedence over broader ones. | Scope | Location | Purpose | Use case examples | Shared with | | ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- | | **Managed policy** | • macOS: `/Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/CLAUDE.md`
• Linux and WSL: `/etc/claude-code/CLAUDE.md`
• Windows: `C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\CLAUDE.md` | Organization-wide instructions managed by IT/DevOps | Company coding standards, security policies, compliance requirements | All users in organization | | **Project instructions** | `./CLAUDE.md` or `./.claude/CLAUDE.md` | Team-shared instructions for the project | Project architecture, coding standards, common workflows | Team members via source control | | **User instructions** | `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` | Personal preferences for all projects | Code styling preferences, personal tooling shortcuts | Just you (all projects) | | **Local instructions** | `./CLAUDE.local.md` | Personal project-specific preferences; add to `.gitignore` | Your sandbox URLs, preferred test data | Just you (current project) | CLAUDE.md and CLAUDE.local.md files in the directory hierarchy above the working directory are loaded in full at launch. Files in subdirectories load on demand when Claude reads files in those directories. See [How CLAUDE.md files load](#how-claude-md-files-load) for the full resolution order. For large projects, you can break instructions into topic-specific files using [project rules](#organize-rules-with-claude/rules/). Rules let you scope instructions to specific file types or subdirectories. ### Set up a project CLAUDE.md A project CLAUDE.md can be stored in either `./CLAUDE.md` or `./.claude/CLAUDE.md`. Create this file and add instructions that apply to anyone working on the project: build and test commands, coding standards, architectural decisions, naming conventions, and common workflows. These instructions are shared with your team through version control, so focus on project-level standards rather than personal preferences. Run `/init` to generate a starting CLAUDE.md automatically. Claude analyzes your codebase and creates a file with build commands, test instructions, and project conventions it discovers. If a CLAUDE.md already exists, `/init` suggests improvements rather than overwriting it. Refine from there with instructions Claude wouldn't discover on its own. Set `CLAUDE_CODE_NEW_INIT=1` to enable an interactive multi-phase flow. `/init` asks which artifacts to set up: CLAUDE.md files, skills, and hooks. It then explores your codebase with a subagent, fills in gaps via follow-up questions, and presents a reviewable proposal before writing any files. ### Write effective instructions CLAUDE.md files are loaded into the context window at the start of every session, consuming tokens alongside your conversation. The [context window visualization](/en/context-window) shows where CLAUDE.md loads relative to the rest of the startup context. Because they're context rather than enforced configuration, how you write instructions affects how reliably Claude follows them. Specific, concise, well-structured instructions work best. **Size**: target under 200 lines per CLAUDE.md file. Longer files consume more context and reduce adherence. If your instructions are growing large, split them using [imports](#import-additional-files) or [`.claude/rules/`](#organize-rules-with-claude/rules/) files. **Structure**: use markdown headers and bullets to group related instructions. Claude scans structure the same way readers do: organized sections are easier to follow than dense paragraphs. **Specificity**: write instructions that are concrete enough to verify. For example: * "Use 2-space indentation" instead of "Format code properly" * "Run `npm test` before committing" instead of "Test your changes" * "API handlers live in `src/api/handlers/`" instead of "Keep files organized" **Consistency**: if two rules contradict each other, Claude may pick one arbitrarily. Review your CLAUDE.md files, nested CLAUDE.md files in subdirectories, and [`.claude/rules/`](#organize-rules-with-claude/rules/) periodically to remove outdated or conflicting instructions. In monorepos, use [`claudeMdExcludes`](#exclude-specific-claude-md-files) to skip CLAUDE.md files from other teams that aren't relevant to your work. ### Import additional files CLAUDE.md files can import additional files using `@path/to/import` syntax. Imported files are expanded and loaded into context at launch alongside the CLAUDE.md that references them. Both relative and absolute paths are allowed. Relative paths resolve relative to the file containing the import, not the working directory. Imported files can recursively import other files, with a maximum depth of five hops. To pull in a README, package.json, and a workflow guide, reference them with `@` syntax anywhere in your CLAUDE.md: ```text theme={null} See @README for project overview and @package.json for available npm commands for this project. # Additional Instructions - git workflow @docs/git-instructions.md ``` For private per-project preferences that shouldn't be checked into version control, create a `CLAUDE.local.md` at the project root. It loads alongside `CLAUDE.md` and is treated the same way. Add `CLAUDE.local.md` to your `.gitignore` so it isn't committed; running `/init` and choosing the personal option does this for you. If you work across multiple git worktrees of the same repository, a gitignored `CLAUDE.local.md` only exists in the worktree where you created it. To share personal instructions across worktrees, import a file from your home directory instead: ```text theme={null} # Individual Preferences - @~/.claude/my-project-instructions.md ``` The first time Claude Code encounters external imports in a project, it shows an approval dialog listing the files. If you decline, the imports stay disabled and the dialog does not appear again. For a more structured approach to organizing instructions, see [`.claude/rules/`](#organize-rules-with-claude/rules/). ### AGENTS.md Claude Code reads `CLAUDE.md`, not `AGENTS.md`. If your repository already uses `AGENTS.md` for other coding agents, create a `CLAUDE.md` that imports it so both tools read the same instructions without duplicating them. You can also add Claude-specific instructions below the import. Claude loads the imported file at session start, then appends the rest: ```markdown CLAUDE.md theme={null} @AGENTS.md ## Claude Code Use plan mode for changes under `src/billing/`. ``` ### How CLAUDE.md files load Claude Code reads CLAUDE.md files by walking up the directory tree from your current working directory, checking each directory along the way for `CLAUDE.md` and `CLAUDE.local.md` files. This means if you run Claude Code in `foo/bar/`, it loads instructions from `foo/bar/CLAUDE.md`, `foo/CLAUDE.md`, and any `CLAUDE.local.md` files alongside them. All discovered files are concatenated into context rather than overriding each other. Within each directory, `CLAUDE.local.md` is appended after `CLAUDE.md`, so when instructions conflict, your personal notes are the last thing Claude reads at that level. Claude also discovers `CLAUDE.md` and `CLAUDE.local.md` files in subdirectories under your current working directory. Instead of loading them at launch, they are included when Claude reads files in those subdirectories. If you work in a large monorepo where other teams' CLAUDE.md files get picked up, use [`claudeMdExcludes`](#exclude-specific-claude-md-files) to skip them. Block-level HTML comments (``) in CLAUDE.md files are stripped before the content is injected into Claude's context. Use them to leave notes for human maintainers without spending context tokens on them. Comments inside code blocks are preserved. When you open a CLAUDE.md file directly with the Read tool, comments remain visible. #### Load from additional directories The `--add-dir` flag gives Claude access to additional directories outside your main working directory. By default, CLAUDE.md files from these directories are not loaded. To also load CLAUDE.md files from additional directories, including `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/CLAUDE.md`, and `.claude/rules/*.md`, set the `CLAUDE_CODE_ADDITIONAL_DIRECTORIES_CLAUDE_MD` environment variable: ```bash theme={null} CLAUDE_CODE_ADDITIONAL_DIRECTORIES_CLAUDE_MD=1 claude --add-dir ../shared-config ``` `CLAUDE.local.md` files in additional directories are not loaded. ### Organize rules with `.claude/rules/` For larger projects, you can organize instructions into multiple files using the `.claude/rules/` directory. This keeps instructions modular and easier for teams to maintain. Rules can also be [scoped to specific file paths](#path-specific-rules), so they only load into context when Claude works with matching files, reducing noise and saving context space. Rules load into context every session or when matching files are opened. For task-specific instructions that don't need to be in context all the time, use [skills](/en/skills) instead, which only load when you invoke them or when Claude determines they're relevant to your prompt. #### Set up rules Place markdown files in your project's `.claude/rules/` directory. Each file should cover one topic, with a descriptive filename like `testing.md` or `api-design.md`. All `.md` files are discovered recursively, so you can organize rules into subdirectories like `frontend/` or `backend/`: ```text theme={null} your-project/ ├── .claude/ │ ├── CLAUDE.md # Main project instructions │ └── rules/ │ ├── code-style.md # Code style guidelines │ ├── testing.md # Testing conventions │ └── security.md # Security requirements ``` Rules without [`paths` frontmatter](#path-specific-rules) are loaded at launch with the same priority as `.claude/CLAUDE.md`. #### Path-specific rules Rules can be scoped to specific files using YAML frontmatter with the `paths` field. These conditional rules only apply when Claude is working with files matching the specified patterns. ```markdown theme={null} --- paths: - "src/api/**/*.ts" --- # API Development Rules - All API endpoints must include input validation - Use the standard error response format - Include OpenAPI documentation comments ``` Rules without a `paths` field are loaded unconditionally and apply to all files. Path-scoped rules trigger when Claude reads files matching the pattern, not on every tool use. Use glob patterns in the `paths` field to match files by extension, directory, or any combination: | Pattern | Matches | | ---------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | | `**/*.ts` | All TypeScript files in any directory | | `src/**/*` | All files under `src/` directory | | `*.md` | Markdown files in the project root | | `src/components/*.tsx` | React components in a specific directory | You can specify multiple patterns and use brace expansion to match multiple extensions in one pattern: ```markdown theme={null} --- paths: - "src/**/*.{ts,tsx}" - "lib/**/*.ts" - "tests/**/*.test.ts" --- ``` #### Share rules across projects with symlinks The `.claude/rules/` directory supports symlinks, so you can maintain a shared set of rules and link them into multiple projects. Symlinks are resolved and loaded normally, and circular symlinks are detected and handled gracefully. This example links both a shared directory and an individual file: ```bash theme={null} ln -s ~/shared-claude-rules .claude/rules/shared ln -s ~/company-standards/security.md .claude/rules/security.md ``` #### User-level rules Personal rules in `~/.claude/rules/` apply to every project on your machine. Use them for preferences that aren't project-specific: ```text theme={null} ~/.claude/rules/ ├── preferences.md # Your personal coding preferences └── workflows.md # Your preferred workflows ``` User-level rules are loaded before project rules, giving project rules higher priority. ### Manage CLAUDE.md for large teams For organizations deploying Claude Code across teams, you can centralize instructions and control which CLAUDE.md files are loaded. #### Deploy organization-wide CLAUDE.md Organizations can deploy a centrally managed CLAUDE.md that applies to all users on a machine. This file cannot be excluded by individual settings. * macOS: `/Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/CLAUDE.md` * Linux and WSL: `/etc/claude-code/CLAUDE.md` * Windows: `C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\CLAUDE.md` Use MDM, Group Policy, Ansible, or similar tools to distribute the file across developer machines. See [managed settings](/en/permissions#managed-settings) for other organization-wide configuration options. A managed CLAUDE.md and [managed settings](/en/settings#settings-files) serve different purposes. Use settings for technical enforcement and CLAUDE.md for behavioral guidance: | Concern | Configure in | | :--------------------------------------------- | :-------------------------------------------------------- | | Block specific tools, commands, or file paths | Managed settings: `permissions.deny` | | Enforce sandbox isolation | Managed settings: `sandbox.enabled` | | Environment variables and API provider routing | Managed settings: `env` | | Authentication method and organization lock | Managed settings: `forceLoginMethod`, `forceLoginOrgUUID` | | Code style and quality guidelines | Managed CLAUDE.md | | Data handling and compliance reminders | Managed CLAUDE.md | | Behavioral instructions for Claude | Managed CLAUDE.md | Settings rules are enforced by the client regardless of what Claude decides to do. CLAUDE.md instructions shape Claude's behavior but are not a hard enforcement layer. #### Exclude specific CLAUDE.md files In large monorepos, ancestor CLAUDE.md files may contain instructions that aren't relevant to your work. The `claudeMdExcludes` setting lets you skip specific files by path or glob pattern. This example excludes a top-level CLAUDE.md and a rules directory from a parent folder. Add it to `.claude/settings.local.json` so the exclusion stays local to your machine: ```json theme={null} { "claudeMdExcludes": [ "**/monorepo/CLAUDE.md", "/home/user/monorepo/other-team/.claude/rules/**" ] } ``` Patterns are matched against absolute file paths using glob syntax. You can configure `claudeMdExcludes` at any [settings layer](/en/settings#settings-files): user, project, local, or managed policy. Arrays merge across layers. Managed policy CLAUDE.md files cannot be excluded. This ensures organization-wide instructions always apply regardless of individual settings. ## Auto memory Auto memory lets Claude accumulate knowledge across sessions without you writing anything. Claude saves notes for itself as it works: build commands, debugging insights, architecture notes, code style preferences, and workflow habits. Claude doesn't save something every session. It decides what's worth remembering based on whether the information would be useful in a future conversation. Auto memory requires Claude Code v2.1.59 or later. Check your version with `claude --version`. ### Enable or disable auto memory Auto memory is on by default. To toggle it, open `/memory` in a session and use the auto memory toggle, or set `autoMemoryEnabled` in your project settings: ```json theme={null} { "autoMemoryEnabled": false } ``` To disable auto memory via environment variable, set `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1`. ### Storage location Each project gets its own memory directory at `~/.claude/projects//memory/`. The `` path is derived from the git repository, so all worktrees and subdirectories within the same repo share one auto memory directory. Outside a git repo, the project root is used instead. To store auto memory in a different location, set `autoMemoryDirectory` in your user or local settings: ```json theme={null} { "autoMemoryDirectory": "~/my-custom-memory-dir" } ``` This setting is accepted from policy, local, and user settings. It is not accepted from project settings (`.claude/settings.json`) to prevent a shared project from redirecting auto memory writes to sensitive locations. The directory contains a `MEMORY.md` entrypoint and optional topic files: ```text theme={null} ~/.claude/projects//memory/ ├── MEMORY.md # Concise index, loaded into every session ├── debugging.md # Detailed notes on debugging patterns ├── api-conventions.md # API design decisions └── ... # Any other topic files Claude creates ``` `MEMORY.md` acts as an index of the memory directory. Claude reads and writes files in this directory throughout your session, using `MEMORY.md` to keep track of what's stored where. Auto memory is machine-local. All worktrees and subdirectories within the same git repository share one auto memory directory. Files are not shared across machines or cloud environments. ### How it works The first 200 lines of `MEMORY.md`, or the first 25KB, whichever comes first, are loaded at the start of every conversation. Content beyond that threshold is not loaded at session start. Claude keeps `MEMORY.md` concise by moving detailed notes into separate topic files. This limit applies only to `MEMORY.md`. CLAUDE.md files are loaded in full regardless of length, though shorter files produce better adherence. Topic files like `debugging.md` or `patterns.md` are not loaded at startup. Claude reads them on demand using its standard file tools when it needs the information. Claude reads and writes memory files during your session. When you see "Writing memory" or "Recalled memory" in the Claude Code interface, Claude is actively updating or reading from `~/.claude/projects//memory/`. ### Audit and edit your memory Auto memory files are plain markdown you can edit or delete at any time. Run [`/memory`](#view-and-edit-with-memory) to browse and open memory files from within a session. ## View and edit with `/memory` The `/memory` command lists all CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE.local.md, and rules files loaded in your current session, lets you toggle auto memory on or off, and provides a link to open the auto memory folder. Select any file to open it in your editor. When you ask Claude to remember something, like "always use pnpm, not npm" or "remember that the API tests require a local Redis instance," Claude saves it to auto memory. To add instructions to CLAUDE.md instead, ask Claude directly, like "add this to CLAUDE.md," or edit the file yourself via `/memory`. ## Troubleshoot memory issues These are the most common issues with CLAUDE.md and auto memory, along with steps to debug them. ### Claude isn't following my CLAUDE.md CLAUDE.md content is delivered as a user message after the system prompt, not as part of the system prompt itself. Claude reads it and tries to follow it, but there's no guarantee of strict compliance, especially for vague or conflicting instructions. To debug: * Run `/memory` to verify your CLAUDE.md and CLAUDE.local.md files are being loaded. If a file isn't listed, Claude can't see it. * Check that the relevant CLAUDE.md is in a location that gets loaded for your session (see [Choose where to put CLAUDE.md files](#choose-where-to-put-claude-md-files)). * Make instructions more specific. "Use 2-space indentation" works better than "format code nicely." * Look for conflicting instructions across CLAUDE.md files. If two files give different guidance for the same behavior, Claude may pick one arbitrarily. For instructions you want at the system prompt level, use [`--append-system-prompt`](/en/cli-reference#system-prompt-flags). This must be passed every invocation, so it's better suited to scripts and automation than interactive use. Use the [`InstructionsLoaded` hook](/en/hooks#instructionsloaded) to log exactly which instruction files are loaded, when they load, and why. This is useful for debugging path-specific rules or lazy-loaded files in subdirectories. ### I don't know what auto memory saved Run `/memory` and select the auto memory folder to browse what Claude has saved. Everything is plain markdown you can read, edit, or delete. ### My CLAUDE.md is too large Files over 200 lines consume more context and may reduce adherence. Move detailed content into separate files referenced with `@path` imports (see [Import additional files](#import-additional-files)), or split your instructions across `.claude/rules/` files. ### Instructions seem lost after `/compact` Project-root CLAUDE.md survives compaction: after `/compact`, Claude re-reads it from disk and re-injects it into the session. Nested CLAUDE.md files in subdirectories are not re-injected automatically; they reload the next time Claude reads a file in that subdirectory. If an instruction disappeared after compaction, it was either given only in conversation or lives in a nested CLAUDE.md that hasn't reloaded yet. Add conversation-only instructions to CLAUDE.md to make them persist. See [What survives compaction](/en/context-window#what-survives-compaction) for the full breakdown. See [Write effective instructions](#write-effective-instructions) for guidance on size, structure, and specificity. ## Related resources * [Skills](/en/skills): package repeatable workflows that load on demand * [Settings](/en/settings): configure Claude Code behavior with settings files * [Subagent memory](/en/sub-agents#enable-persistent-memory): let subagents maintain their own auto memory 이건 어떻게 클로드개 내 프로젝트를 기억하고 있는지에 대한 내용이야. 이걸 바탕으로 토큰 최적화 및 더 좋은 작업을 위한 방향을 위한 수정 방안이 있을까

# NINEONELABS Renewal Project

## Build Commands

```bash
npm run build        # Production build (JS + CSS)
npm run watch        # Dev mode (auto rebuild)
npm run build:css    # Compile SCSS only
make up              # Start Docker containers
make down            # Remove containers
make bash            # Access web container
make migrate         # Run DB migrations
make migrate-status  # Check migration status
make install         # Install npm + composer packages
```

## Stack

- **Backend**: PHP 7.4, Custom MVC framework, MySQL 8.0, Apache (Docker)
- **Frontend**: TypeScript, SCSS, Three.js, Vite, Swiper
- **Packages**: Composer (PHP), npm (Node.js, runs locally)

## Naming Conventions

- **Classes**: PascalCase (e.g. `Application`, `Router`)
- **Methods/Variables**: camelCase (e.g. `handleRequest()`, `$request`)
- **Constants**: UPPER_SNAKE_CASE (e.g. `ROOT_PATH`, `DEFAULT_LOCALE`)
- **DB Tables**: `nb_` prefix (e.g. `nb_siteinfo`, `nb_admin`)
- **SCSS**: BEM pattern

## Architecture Patterns

```php
// Routing
$router->get('/', function () {
    return render('pages.index');
})->name('home');

// View rendering
render('pages.index');                          // views/pages/index.php
render('pages.works.view', ['no' => $no]);      // views/pages/works/view.php
```

## Namespaces

- `Core\` — Application core
- `Database\` — Database layer
- `Http\` — Request/Response
- `Routing\` — Router
- `View\` — View engine
- `Menu\` — Menu system

## Workflow Rules

- Do NOT run `npm run build` or `npm run watch` — the dev server is always running and reflects changes on save automatically
- Do NOT suggest starting the dev server; assume it is already running
- DB schema changes must go through migration files (`make m`)
- `vendor/` must be included in deployment; exclude `node_modules/`
- SCSS source: `resource/scss/` → compiled output: `resource/dist/`

- phpMyAdmin: [http://localhost:8081](http://localhost:8081)

You are a senior TypeScript engineer. Refactor this Three.js global web project.

## CONSTRAINTS

### Architecture

- OOP + SOLID. SRP per class. No God Objects
- No nested if. Guard clauses or strategy/lookup only
- No side effects outside service boundaries
- No dead code, unused imports, unused variables

### Naming & Polymorphism

- Format: [Class].[verb] — Earth.show(), Arc.update(), Marker.dispose()
- No verb-stacking: handleEarthVisibilityChange() → Earth.show()
- Interface-driven polymorphism: Renderable.render(), Disposable.dispose(), Resizable.resize()

### Types & Config

- All types/interfaces/enums → \*.types.ts only. No inline types. No `any`
- All constants, colors, sizes, URLs → config files only. No magic numbers

### Three.js

- API as documented. No monkey-patching
- dispose() required for every geometry, material, texture
- No object creation inside render loop
- addEventListener must have matching removeEventListener
- Minimize draw calls. Use instancing or merged geometry where applicable
- Update uniforms/attributes only when necessary

### Encoding

- All files must be saved as UTF-8 without BOM
- Korean characters must never be escaped or mangled
- No \uXXXX escape sequences for Korean strings in source code
- TextDecoder/TextEncoder must explicitly specify 'utf-8'

### Files

- Read every .ts file before changing anything
- Merge files where SRP allows. Delete unused files
- No new files without explicit justification

### Error Handling

- No silent catch. No unhandled Promise rejections

## OUTPUT

1. Violations: [file] — [rule] — [problem]
2. Final file structure
3. Full file contents. No partial diffs under 300 lines

## TONE

No compliments. Violations and fixes only.

## PROJECT

- Stack: Three.js + TypeScript, [Vite/Webpack]
- Entry: [main.ts]
- Known issues: [or remove this line]

content.content:
1	# ROLE
2	
3	Last audited: 2026-04-05  
4	Scope: repo-wide contract for **public PHP + TypeScript + Three.js**, **SCSS token ownership**, **HTML view rendering**, **API/data helpers for works**, **admin PHP/JS split**, and **runtime boundaries**.
5	
6	---
7	
8	## 1. Project shape
9	
10	### 1.1 Stack and responsibilities
11	
12	- **PHP (public app)**: HTTP entry resolves through `src/autoload.php` → `Core\Application` → `routes/web.php` closures. Pages are **not** classic controller-class MVC on the public site.
13	- **TypeScript + Three.js**: Compiled/bundled from `resource/ts/`; `resource/ts/app.ts` is the browser entry. Heavy 3D lives on managed pages (`main`, `about`, `contact`); `works` uses a **lazy-loaded** dedicated runtime.
14	- **SCSS (public)**: `resource/scss/style.scss` is the single public stylesheet entry (see §3).
15	- **Admin**: Separate tree under `admin/` (controllers, models, `pages/`, `resource/`). Styles/scripts are **not** the same chain as public `resource/scss` (see §2.3).
16	- **Database**: MySQL-oriented; connection via `src/Database/DB.php` and legacy `inc/lib/db.php` paths used from older includes. Schema snapshots and ad-hoc SQL live under `database/`; repeatable changes should prefer `database/migrations/*.sql` (and PHP migrations under `src/Database/migrations/` when used).
17	- **Docker**: `docker-compose.yml` provides `web` (PHP/Apache), `db` (MySQL 8), `phpmyadmin` for local parity—not required for the architecture contract, but documents the default dev topology.
18	
19	### 1.2 Primary public routes vs runtime `pageType`
20	
21	| Path (prefix) | Typical `pageType` / namespace | TS strategy (see §5) |
22	|---------------|-------------------------------|----------------------|
23	| `/` | `main` | `ManagedPageStrategy` → `AppManager` |
24	| `/about` | `about` | Managed |
25	| `/contact` | `contact` | Managed |
26	| `/works` | `works`, `works-index` | `LazyRuntimePageStrategy` → `WorksPageRuntime` |
27	| `/works/view/{no}` | `works-view` | `NoopPageStrategy` (modal/shell driven) |
28	| `/works/modal/{no}` | `works-modal` | Noop |
29	| `/careers` | `careers` | **Noop** unless a `PAGE_STRATEGIES` entry is added (subpages use global `PageRuntime` UI only) |
30	| `/inside/*` | `inside` (all inside routes, including `/inside/award`) | **Noop** today — no `inside` key in `PAGE_STRATEGIES`; three.js page init is skipped |
31	| `/legal/privacy`, `/legal/terms` | `legal` | Noop (static/legal shell) |
32	
33	**Note:** [`resource/ts/core/setup.ts`](../resource/ts/core/setup.ts) defines `pageAward` as a constant, but [`routes/web.php`](../routes/web.php) currently passes `'pageType' => 'inside'` for `/inside/award`, so `main[data-page]` is `inside`, not `award`. The `PAGE_STRATEGIES[pageAward]` branch (`StaticInitPageStrategy` / `ImagePreview`) only runs if a view/route sets `pageType` to match that id.
34	
35	Exact `data-page` / `pageType` values must stay aligned with [`resource/ts/controller/PageController.ts`](../resource/ts/controller/PageController.ts) and [`resource/ts/app/EnvSetup.ts`](../resource/ts/app/EnvSetup.ts) (or equivalent).
36	
37	### 1.3 Works data boundary
38	
39	- **Server-side helpers** for listing/detail/categories are loaded from [`api/works.php`](../api/works.php) when routes need them (see [`routes/web.php`](../routes/web.php): `$loadWorksApi`).
40	- **JSON pagination** for infinite scroll: `GET /works/list` returns `{ items, nextOffset, hasMore }`.
41	- **Partial HTML** for modal: `GET /works/modal-component/{no}` returns `include_view('components.work-modal', …)` as HTML fragment.
42	
43	### 1.4 Contact submission
44	
45	- `GET /contact` renders [`views/pages/contact/index.php`](../views/pages/contact/index.php) with option arrays from globals.
46	- `POST /contact` includes [`module/request.php`](../module/request.php) and returns JSON via `contact_request_process_submit()` (see route in [`routes/web.php`](../routes/web.php)).
47	
48	---
49	
50	## 2. Request pipeline and “MVC”
51	
52	### 2.1 Public frontend (closure routes + view engine)
53	
54	- **Not** a controller-class MVC for public pages.
55	- **Flow**:
56	  1. [`src/autoload.php`](../src/autoload.php) — loads Composer if present, `config/setup.php`, `config/helpers.php`, registers PSR-4-style autoload for `src/*`, constructs `Application`, **skips** `routes/web.php` when the path is under the resolved admin directory (see `AdminDirectoryResolver`).
57	  2. [`routes/web.php`](../routes/web.php) — registers routes; handlers call `render('pages.*', $data)` or `Response::json()`.
58	  3. [`config/helpers.php`](../config/helpers.php) — `render()`, `include_view()`, `response()`, `app()` helpers.
59	  4. [`src/View/ViewEngine.php`](../src/View/ViewEngine.php) — resolves dot-notation view names, applies layout, passes data.
60	  5. [`views/layouts/main.php`](../views/layouts/main.php) — site chrome; pages pull fragments via `include_view('components.*')`.
61	
62	### 2.2 Core PHP namespaces (`src/`)
63	
64	- **`Core\Application`**: request/response, router, lightweight service container, dispatch lifecycle.
65	- **`Http\Request` / `Http\Response`**: abstraction over superglobals and headers/body.
66	- **`Routing\Router`**: groups, named routes, parameter extraction (used from `routes/web.php` via `app()->router()`).
67	- **`View\ViewEngine`**: layout + partial rendering contract.
68	- **`Database\DB`**: DB access for modern code paths.
69	- **`Bootstrap\*`**: cross-cutting boot concerns (`AdminDirectoryResolver`, `SessionContext`, `ErrorHandler`, `LicenseValidator`, `UploadPathRegistry`, etc.) — used from legacy `inc/lib/base.class.php` and newer entrypoints.
70	- **`Admin\Auth\*`**: admin authentication/session/role helpers when referenced from admin bootstrap.
71	
72	**Rule**: New **public** features should prefer `src/` classes and `routes/web.php`; avoid growing one-off `inc/lib` entrypoints unless integrating with legacy admin includes.
73	
74	### 2.3 Admin (explicit Controller / Model / pages)
75	
76	- **Physical layout**:
77	  - [`admin/Controller/*.php`](../admin/Controller/) — request handling, orchestration, JSON responses for JS clients.
78	  - [`admin/Model/*.php`](../admin/Model/) — DB queries and domain rules per resource (e.g. `WorkModel`, `BoardModel`).
79	  - [`admin/pages/**/*.php`](../admin/pages/) — HTML UI fragments; included from router/front controller pattern in `admin/index.php` (and related).
80	  - [`admin/resource/js/`](../admin/resource/js/) — ES modules: `Controller/*Controller.js`, `core/*`, `utils/*`; loaded by admin pages.
81	  - [`admin/resource/css/style.css`](../admin/resource/css/style.css) — compiled or hand-maintained admin skin; linked from [`admin/inc/admin.css.php`](../admin/inc/admin.css.php) as `NO_ADMIN_RESOURCE_BASE`.
82	  - [`admin/config/menu.config.php`](../admin/config/menu.config.php) — navigation source of truth for drawer/sections.
83	  - [`admin/lib/`](../admin/lib/) — shared admin PHP (`PageContext`, validators, pagination, auth includes under `admin/lib/auth/`, etc.).
84	
85	- **Do not** project admin Controller/Model conventions onto **public** `routes/web.php` handlers.
86	
87	### 2.4 Legacy bridge (`inc/lib`)
88	
89	- [`inc/lib/base.class.php`](../inc/lib/base.class.php) remains the **admin (and some legacy) bootstrap** surface: session, error reporting, license checks, upload path registry, `ROOT_PATH` discovery via `no_find_project_root()`.
90	- Other `inc/lib/*.php` files (e.g. `func.php`, `var.php`, `board.class.php`) support **older** includes and admin pages. When adding features, **prefer** `src/` + explicit routes unless the change must live inside an existing legacy include chain.
91	
92	---
93	
94	## 3. SCSS structure (public site)
95	
96	### 3.1 Entry chain
97	
98	- [`resource/scss/style.scss`](../resource/scss/style.scss)
99	  - `@use "./base"`
100	  - `@use "./layouts"`
101	  - `@use "./components"`
102	  - `@use "./pages"`
103	
104	### 3.2 Layer ownership
105	
106	- **`resource/scss/abstract`** — Sass-only tokens: maps, functions, mixins, type scales. Examples: [`_colors.scss`](../resource/scss/abstract/_colors.scss), [`_variables.scss`](../resource/scss/abstract/_variables.scss), [`_headings.scss`](../resource/scss/abstract/_headings.scss), [`_mixins.scss`](../resource/scss/abstract/_mixins.scss), [`_functions.scss`](../resource/scss/abstract/_functions.scss).
107	- **`resource/scss/base`** — CSS custom properties, reset, global init, utilities consumed at runtime. Examples: [`_root.scss`](../resource/scss/base/_root.scss), [`_reset.scss`](../resource/scss/base/_reset.scss), [`_init.scss`](../resource/scss/base/_init.scss), [`_utils.scss`](../resource/scss/base/_utils.scss).
108	- **`resource/scss/components`** — reusable UI; must **consume** tokens, not redefine global semantics.
109	- **`resource/scss/layouts`** — header, drawer, footer, shell-level layout.
110	- **`resource/scss/pages`** — page-only layout and motion; no new global design language.
111	
112	### 3.3 Token contract
113	
114	- Reusable semantic tokens → `abstract` or `base/_root.scss`.
115	- Components → `var(--clr-*)`, `var(--duration-*)`, `var(--ease-*)`, `fluid(...)`, `@include font(...)` etc. directly.
116	- **Forbidden**: `$alias` that only wraps an existing root token; duplicating `--clr-*` / motion tokens in consumer layers; raw hex in consumers when semantic color exists upstream.
117	
118	### 3.4 Admin styles
119	
120	- Admin CSS is **out of scope** for the public SCSS token contract unless explicitly sharing variables (generally **avoid** coupling). Admin changes belong in `admin/resource/css/` and related includes.
121	
122	---
123	
124	## 4. HTML view structure
125	
126	### 4.1 Ownership
127	
128	- **`views/layouts/`** — outer chrome; primary public layout: [`views/layouts/main.php`](../views/layouts/main.php).
129	- **`views/pages/`** — route bodies. Examples:
130	  - [`views/pages/index.php`](../views/pages/index.php) — home.
131	  - [`views/pages/about/index.php`](../views/pages/about/index.php).
132	  - [`views/pages/contact/index.php`](../views/pages/contact/index.php).
133	  - [`views/pages/works/`](../views/pages/works/) — index, view, modal templates for works.
134	  - [`views/pages/careers/`](../views/pages/careers/), [`views/pages/inside/`](../views/pages/inside/), [`views/pages/legal/`](../views/pages/legal/) — section pages.
135	- **`views/components/`** — fragments: navigation, work modal, cards, etc. Any reusable markup must live here and be included with `include_view('components.*')`.
136	
137	### 4.2 Render contract
138	
139	- Handlers return `render('pages.*', $data)` for full pages.
140	- Layout selection is owned by the view engine, not duplicated in page templates.
141	- Page templates **must not** re-encode site chrome already provided by `layouts/main.php`.
142	- For **HTML partials** (e.g. modal content), return `response(include_view(...), 200, ['Content-Type' => 'text/html; charset=UTF-8'])` when appropriate.
143	
144	---
145	
146	## 5. TypeScript + Three.js core
147	
148	### 5.1 Bootstrap chain (public)
149	
150	1. [`resource/ts/app.ts`](../resource/ts/app.ts) — browser entry.
151	2. [`resource/ts/core/AppBootstrap.ts`](../resource/ts/core/AppBootstrap.ts) — wires `LenisRuntime` + [`resource/ts/runtime/PageRuntime.ts`](../resource/ts/runtime/PageRuntime.ts); queries `main[data-page]`.
152	3. [`resource/ts/runtime/PageRuntime.ts`](../resource/ts/runtime/PageRuntime.ts) — global UI (drawer, header, cursor, reveals, contact wizard, work modal host, etc.) and delegates **page** init to [`resource/ts/controller/PageController.ts`](../resource/ts/controller/PageController.ts).
153	4. [`resource/ts/controller/PageController.ts`](../resource/ts/controller/PageController.ts) — **strategy per `pageType`**:
154	   - **`ManagedPageStrategy`** — `main`, `about`, `contact`: loads scene config from [`resource/ts/pages/*/scene/*.scene.ts`](../resource/ts/pages/), runs [`resource/ts/manager/AppManager.ts`](../resource/ts/manager/AppManager.ts).
155	   - **`LazyRuntimePageStrategy`** — `works`: dynamic `import('../pages/works/runtime/WorksPageRuntime.js')`.
156	   - **`StaticInitPageStrategy`** — keyed by `pageAward` in code; only runs if `data-page` equals that id (see §1.2 note on `/inside/award`).
157	   - **`NoopPageStrategy`** — `works-view`, `works-modal`, `legal`, etc., when Three/global page orchestration is not required.
158	
159	### 5.2 Engine and shared runtime
160	
161	- [`resource/ts/core/Engine.ts`](../resource/ts/core/Engine.ts), [`resource/ts/core/setup.ts`](../resource/ts/core/setup.ts) — scene/object ids, layer constants, page id constants (`pageMain`, `pageWorks`, `pageContact`, `pageLegal`, …).
162	- [`resource/ts/runtime/*`](../resource/ts/runtime/) — timeline, scroll scenes, transitions, intro flows, app engine runtime, starfield, etc.
163	- [`resource/ts/core/PageTheatreBinder.ts`](../resource/ts/core/PageTheatreBinder.ts) — **lazy theatre** boundary; page-specific theatre under `resource/ts/pages/<page>/theatre/`.
164	- **Theatre savefiles** — [`resource/json/*.json`](../resource/json/).
165	
166	### 5.3 Works-specific layout
167	
168	Under [`resource/ts/pages/works/`](../resource/ts/pages/works/):
169	
170	- **`runtime/WorksPageRuntime.ts`** — entry orchestration for the works page.
171	- **`scene/works.scene.ts`** — scene declaration for works.
172	- **`theatre/`** — `WorksTheatreConfig.ts`, `WorksTheatreRuntime.ts`, `WorksTheatreBridge.ts`, etc.
173	- **`render/WorksSceneManager.ts`** — scene management/rendering concerns.
174	
175	**Rule**: Do not move generic engine concerns into `pages/works/`; keep page folder for works-only glue, scene, and theatre.
176	
177	### 5.4 Types and config
178	
179	- Shared domain types → [`resource/ts/types/*.types.ts`](../resource/ts/types/).
180	- DOM/GSAP/component configs → [`resource/ts/config/`](../resource/ts/config/).
181	
182	### 5.5 Contact flow ownership
183	
184	- Contact is a **managed** page: intro / ready / outtro / success stages are orchestrated through `AppManager` and contact theatre config under [`resource/ts/pages/contact/theatre/`](../resource/ts/pages/contact/theatre/) (constants imported from `ContactTheatreConfig.js` in `AppManager.ts`).
185	- Do not reintroduce **parallel** contact stage ownership outside this pipeline.
186	
187	---
188	
189	## 6. Configuration and environment
190	
191	- **[`config/setup.php`](../config/setup.php)** — defines `ROOT_PATH`, loads `.env` if present, sets error reporting, session, locale list, and includes `config/project.php` / `config/configuration.php` as applicable.
192	- **[`config/project.php`](../config/project.php)** — project-specific constants (e.g. admin directory name, upload bases). **`AdminDirectoryResolver`** uses this to detect admin requests in `src/autoload.php`.
193	- **[`config/helpers.php`](../config/helpers.php)** — view/render helpers; keep render paths stable for TS `data-page` expectations.
194	- **`.env` / `.env.example`** — environment-specific secrets and flags; never commit secrets.
195	
196	---
197	
198	## 7. Change rules
199	
200	### 7.1 SCSS (public)
201	
202	- Before adding a token, search: `abstract/_colors.scss`, `abstract/_variables.scss`, `abstract/_headings.scss`, `base/_root.scss`.
203	- Reuse if meaning exists; add to shared layer if reusable; keep truly one-off values local (comment only if non-obvious).
204	
205	### 7.2 PHP views
206	
207	- No bypassing the view engine for normal pages.
208	- No moving layout chrome into `views/pages/*`.
209	- Extract reusable markup to `views/components/*`.
210	
211	### 7.3 TypeScript / Three.js
212	
213	- Prefer **config-driven** assembly for managed pages.
214	- Page theatre → `resource/ts/pages/<page>/theatre`.
215	- Page scene → `resource/ts/pages/<page>/scene`.
216	- Shared engine/runtime code stays out of page folders.
217	- New cross-page types → `resource/ts/types/*.types.ts`.
218	
219	### 7.4 Routes and APIs
220	
221	- New **public** GET pages → `routes/web.php` + `views/pages/*` + `render()`.
222	- New **JSON** endpoints → `Http\Response::json()` (or `response()` helper) with explicit status and shape; avoid mixing HTML and JSON handlers in the same closure without clear naming.
223	- **Works-related** list/detail/category behavior → extend [`api/works.php`](../api/works.php) and keep routes thin.
224	
225	### 7.5 Admin
226	
227	- New CRUD surfaces → `admin/Controller`, `admin/Model`, `admin/pages`, `admin/resource/js/Controller`, and menu entry in `admin/config/menu.config.php` when the item should appear in navigation.
228	- Respect existing JSON response patterns expected by admin JS (see `admin/resource/js/core/fetcher.js` and per-controller JS).
229	
230	---
231	
232	## 8. Prohibited changes
233	
234	- Reintroducing **deprecated** assumptions:
235	  - Public **controller-class** MVC for marketing pages.
236	  - **Barba** (or similar) as the primary navigation/runtime contract.
237	  - Component-local Sass aliases duplicating root tokens.
238	- Duplicating ownership already centralized in **`AppManager`**, **`PageRuntime`**, or **`PageTheatreBinder`**.

240	
241	---
242	
243	## 9. Document ownership
244	
245	- **This file** (`docs/ROLE.MD`) is the repo-wide **architecture contract** for boundaries above.
246	- **[`docs/TS_FLOW.md`](TS_FLOW.md)** — runtime execution order and flow details.
247	- **[`docs/TS_CORE.md`](TS_CORE.md)** — TypeScript layering, ownership, and extension rules.

# ROLE

Last audited: 2026-04-05  
Scope: repo-wide contract for **public PHP + TypeScript + Three.js**, **SCSS token ownership**, **HTML view rendering**, **API/data helpers for works**, **admin PHP/JS split**, and **runtime boundaries**.

---

## 1. Project shape

### 1.1 Stack and responsibilities

- **PHP (public app)**: HTTP entry resolves through `src/autoload.php` → `Core\Application` → `routes/web.php` closures. Pages are **not** classic controller-class MVC on the public site.
- **TypeScript + Three.js**: Compiled/bundled from `resource/ts/`; `resource/ts/app.ts` is the browser entry. Heavy 3D lives on managed pages (`main`, `about`, `contact`); `works` uses a **lazy-loaded** dedicated runtime.
- **SCSS (public)**: `resource/scss/style.scss` is the single public stylesheet entry (see §3).
- **Admin**: Separate tree under `admin/` (controllers, models, `pages/`, `resource/`). Styles/scripts are **not** the same chain as public `resource/scss` (see §2.3).
- **Database**: MySQL-oriented; connection via `src/Database/DB.php` and legacy `inc/lib/db.php` paths used from older includes. Schema snapshots and ad-hoc SQL live under `database/`; repeatable changes should prefer `database/migrations/*.sql` (and PHP migrations under `src/Database/migrations/` when used).
- **Docker**: `docker-compose.yml` provides `web` (PHP/Apache), `db` (MySQL 8), `phpmyadmin` for local parity—not required for the architecture contract, but documents the default dev topology.

### 1.2 Primary public routes vs runtime `pageType`

| Path (prefix) | Typical `pageType` / namespace | TS strategy (see §5) |
|---------------|-------------------------------|----------------------|
| `/` | `main` | `ManagedPageStrategy` → `AppManager` |
| `/about` | `about` | Managed |
| `/contact` | `contact` | Managed |
| `/works` | `works`, `works-index` | `LazyRuntimePageStrategy` → `WorksPageRuntime` |
| `/works/view/{no}` | `works-view` | `NoopPageStrategy` (modal/shell driven) |
| `/works/modal/{no}` | `works-modal` | Noop |
| `/careers` | `careers` | **Noop** unless a `PAGE_STRATEGIES` entry is added (subpages use global `PageRuntime` UI only) |
| `/inside/*` | `inside` (all inside routes, including `/inside/award`) | **Noop** today — no `inside` key in `PAGE_STRATEGIES`; three.js page init is skipped |
| `/legal/privacy`, `/legal/terms` | `legal` | Noop (static/legal shell) |

**Note:** [`resource/ts/core/setup.ts`](../resource/ts/core/setup.ts) defines `pageAward` as a constant, but [`routes/web.php`](../routes/web.php) currently passes `'pageType' => 'inside'` for `/inside/award`, so `main[data-page]` is `inside`, not `award`. The `PAGE_STRATEGIES[pageAward]` branch (`StaticInitPageStrategy` / `ImagePreview`) only runs if a view/route sets `pageType` to match that id.

Exact `data-page` / `pageType` values must stay aligned with [`resource/ts/controller/PageController.ts`](../resource/ts/controller/PageController.ts) and [`resource/ts/app/EnvSetup.ts`](../resource/ts/app/EnvSetup.ts) (or equivalent).

### 1.3 Works data boundary

- **Server-side helpers** for listing/detail/categories are loaded from [`api/works.php`](../api/works.php) when routes need them (see [`routes/web.php`](../routes/web.php): `$loadWorksApi`).
- **JSON pagination** for infinite scroll: `GET /works/list` returns `{ items, nextOffset, hasMore }`.
- **Partial HTML** for modal: `GET /works/modal-component/{no}` returns `include_view('components.work-modal', …)` as HTML fragment.

### 1.4 Contact submission

- `GET /contact` renders [`views/pages/contact/index.php`](../views/pages/contact/index.php) with option arrays from globals.
- `POST /contact` includes [`module/request.php`](../module/request.php) and returns JSON via `contact_request_process_submit()` (see route in [`routes/web.php`](../routes/web.php)).

---

## 2. Request pipeline and “MVC”

### 2.1 Public frontend (closure routes + view engine)

- **Not** a controller-class MVC for public pages.
- **Flow**:
  1. [`src/autoload.php`](../src/autoload.php) — loads Composer if present, `config/setup.php`, `config/helpers.php`, registers PSR-4-style autoload for `src/*`, constructs `Application`, **skips** `routes/web.php` when the path is under the resolved admin directory (see `AdminDirectoryResolver`).
  2. [`routes/web.php`](../routes/web.php) — registers routes; handlers call `render('pages.*', $data)` or `Response::json()`.
  3. [`config/helpers.php`](../config/helpers.php) — `render()`, `include_view()`, `response()`, `app()` helpers.
  4. [`src/View/ViewEngine.php`](../src/View/ViewEngine.php) — resolves dot-notation view names, applies layout, passes data.
  5. [`views/layouts/main.php`](../views/layouts/main.php) — site chrome; pages pull fragments via `include_view('components.*')`.

### 2.2 Core PHP namespaces (`src/`)

- **`Core\Application`**: request/response, router, lightweight service container, dispatch lifecycle.
- **`Http\Request` / `Http\Response`**: abstraction over superglobals and headers/body.
- **`Routing\Router`**: groups, named routes, parameter extraction (used from `routes/web.php` via `app()->router()`).
- **`View\ViewEngine`**: layout + partial rendering contract.
- **`Database\DB`**: DB access for modern code paths.
- **`Bootstrap\*`**: cross-cutting boot concerns (`AdminDirectoryResolver`, `SessionContext`, `ErrorHandler`, `LicenseValidator`, `UploadPathRegistry`, etc.) — used from legacy `inc/lib/base.class.php` and newer entrypoints.
- **`Admin\Auth\*`**: admin authentication/session/role helpers when referenced from admin bootstrap.

**Rule**: New **public** features should prefer `src/` classes and `routes/web.php`; avoid growing one-off `inc/lib` entrypoints unless integrating with legacy admin includes.

### 2.3 Admin (explicit Controller / Model / pages)

- **Physical layout**:
  - [`admin/Controller/*.php`](../admin/Controller/) — request handling, orchestration, JSON responses for JS clients.
  - [`admin/Model/*.php`](../admin/Model/) — DB queries and domain rules per resource (e.g. `WorkModel`, `BoardModel`).
  - [`admin/pages/**/*.php`](../admin/pages/) — HTML UI fragments; included from router/front controller pattern in `admin/index.php` (and related).
  - [`admin/resource/js/`](../admin/resource/js/) — ES modules: `Controller/*Controller.js`, `core/*`, `utils/*`; loaded by admin pages.
  - [`admin/resource/css/style.css`](../admin/resource/css/style.css) — compiled or hand-maintained admin skin; linked from [`admin/inc/admin.css.php`](../admin/inc/admin.css.php) as `NO_ADMIN_RESOURCE_BASE`.
  - [`admin/config/menu.config.php`](../admin/config/menu.config.php) — navigation source of truth for drawer/sections.
  - [`admin/lib/`](../admin/lib/) — shared admin PHP (`PageContext`, validators, pagination, auth includes under `admin/lib/auth/`, etc.).

- **Do not** project admin Controller/Model conventions onto **public** `routes/web.php` handlers.

### 2.4 Legacy bridge (`inc/lib`)

- [`inc/lib/base.class.php`](../inc/lib/base.class.php) remains the **admin (and some legacy) bootstrap** surface: session, error reporting, license checks, upload path registry, `ROOT_PATH` discovery via `no_find_project_root()`.
- Other `inc/lib/*.php` files (e.g. `func.php`, `var.php`, `board.class.php`) support **older** includes and admin pages. When adding features, **prefer** `src/` + explicit routes unless the change must live inside an existing legacy include chain.

---

## 3. SCSS structure (public site)

### 3.1 Entry chain

- [`resource/scss/style.scss`](../resource/scss/style.scss)
  - `@use "./base"`
  - `@use "./layouts"`
  - `@use "./components"`
  - `@use "./pages"`

### 3.2 Layer ownership

- **`resource/scss/abstract`** — Sass-only tokens: maps, functions, mixins, type scales. Examples: [`_colors.scss`](../resource/scss/abstract/_colors.scss), [`_variables.scss`](../resource/scss/abstract/_variables.scss), [`_headings.scss`](../resource/scss/abstract/_headings.scss), [`_mixins.scss`](../resource/scss/abstract/_mixins.scss), [`_functions.scss`](../resource/scss/abstract/_functions.scss).
- **`resource/scss/base`** — CSS custom properties, reset, global init, utilities consumed at runtime. Examples: [`_root.scss`](../resource/scss/base/_root.scss), [`_reset.scss`](../resource/scss/base/_reset.scss), [`_init.scss`](../resource/scss/base/_init.scss), [`_utils.scss`](../resource/scss/base/_utils.scss).
- **`resource/scss/components`** — reusable UI; must **consume** tokens, not redefine global semantics.
- **`resource/scss/layouts`** — header, drawer, footer, shell-level layout.
- **`resource/scss/pages`** — page-only layout and motion; no new global design language.

### 3.3 Token contract

- Reusable semantic tokens → `abstract` or `base/_root.scss`.
- Components → `var(--clr-*)`, `var(--duration-*)`, `var(--ease-*)`, `fluid(...)`, `@include font(...)` etc. directly.
- **Forbidden**: `$alias` that only wraps an existing root token; duplicating `--clr-*` / motion tokens in consumer layers; raw hex in consumers when semantic color exists upstream.

### 3.4 Admin styles

- Admin CSS is **out of scope** for the public SCSS token contract unless explicitly sharing variables (generally **avoid** coupling). Admin changes belong in `admin/resource/css/` and related includes.

---

## 4. HTML view structure

### 4.1 Ownership

- **`views/layouts/`** — outer chrome; primary public layout: [`views/layouts/main.php`](../views/layouts/main.php).
- **`views/pages/`** — route bodies. Examples:
  - [`views/pages/index.php`](../views/pages/index.php) — home.
  - [`views/pages/about/index.php`](../views/pages/about/index.php).
  - [`views/pages/contact/index.php`](../views/pages/contact/index.php).
  - [`views/pages/works/`](../views/pages/works/) — index, view, modal templates for works.
  - [`views/pages/careers/`](../views/pages/careers/), [`views/pages/inside/`](../views/pages/inside/), [`views/pages/legal/`](../views/pages/legal/) — section pages.
- **`views/components/`** — fragments: navigation, work modal, cards, etc. Any reusable markup must live here and be included with `include_view('components.*')`.

### 4.2 Render contract

- Handlers return `render('pages.*', $data)` for full pages.
- Layout selection is owned by the view engine, not duplicated in page templates.
- Page templates **must not** re-encode site chrome already provided by `layouts/main.php`.
- For **HTML partials** (e.g. modal content), return `response(include_view(...), 200, ['Content-Type' => 'text/html; charset=UTF-8'])` when appropriate.

---

## 5. TypeScript + Three.js core

### 5.1 Bootstrap chain (public)

1. [`resource/ts/app.ts`](../resource/ts/app.ts) — browser entry.
2. [`resource/ts/core/AppBootstrap.ts`](../resource/ts/core/AppBootstrap.ts) — wires `LenisRuntime` + [`resource/ts/runtime/PageRuntime.ts`](../resource/ts/runtime/PageRuntime.ts); queries `main[data-page]`.
3. [`resource/ts/runtime/PageRuntime.ts`](../resource/ts/runtime/PageRuntime.ts) — global UI (drawer, header, cursor, reveals, contact wizard, work modal host, etc.) and delegates **page** init to [`resource/ts/controller/PageController.ts`](../resource/ts/controller/PageController.ts).
4. [`resource/ts/controller/PageController.ts`](../resource/ts/controller/PageController.ts) — **strategy per `pageType`**:
   - **`ManagedPageStrategy`** — `main`, `about`, `contact`: loads scene config from [`resource/ts/pages/*/scene/*.scene.ts`](../resource/ts/pages/), runs [`resource/ts/manager/AppManager.ts`](../resource/ts/manager/AppManager.ts).
   - **`LazyRuntimePageStrategy`** — `works`: dynamic `import('../pages/works/runtime/WorksPageRuntime.js')`.
   - **`StaticInitPageStrategy`** — keyed by `pageAward` in code; only runs if `data-page` equals that id (see §1.2 note on `/inside/award`).
   - **`NoopPageStrategy`** — `works-view`, `works-modal`, `legal`, etc., when Three/global page orchestration is not required.

### 5.2 Engine and shared runtime

- [`resource/ts/core/Engine.ts`](../resource/ts/core/Engine.ts), [`resource/ts/core/setup.ts`](../resource/ts/core/setup.ts) — scene/object ids, layer constants, page id constants (`pageMain`, `pageWorks`, `pageContact`, `pageLegal`, …).
- [`resource/ts/runtime/*`](../resource/ts/runtime/) — timeline, scroll scenes, transitions, intro flows, app engine runtime, starfield, etc.
- [`resource/ts/core/PageTheatreBinder.ts`](../resource/ts/core/PageTheatreBinder.ts) — **lazy theatre** boundary; page-specific theatre under `resource/ts/pages/<page>/theatre/`.
- **Theatre savefiles** — [`resource/json/*.json`](../resource/json/).

### 5.3 Works-specific layout

Under [`resource/ts/pages/works/`](../resource/ts/pages/works/):

- **`runtime/WorksPageRuntime.ts`** — entry orchestration for the works page.
- **`scene/works.scene.ts`** — scene declaration for works.
- **`theatre/`** — `WorksTheatreConfig.ts`, `WorksTheatreRuntime.ts`, `WorksTheatreBridge.ts`, etc.
- **`render/WorksSceneManager.ts`** — scene management/rendering concerns.

**Rule**: Do not move generic engine concerns into `pages/works/`; keep page folder for works-only glue, scene, and theatre.

### 5.4 Types and config

- Shared domain types → [`resource/ts/types/*.types.ts`](../resource/ts/types/).
- DOM/GSAP/component configs → [`resource/ts/config/`](../resource/ts/config/).

### 5.5 Contact flow ownership

- Contact is a **managed** page: intro / ready / outtro / success stages are orchestrated through `AppManager` and contact theatre config under [`resource/ts/pages/contact/theatre/`](../resource/ts/pages/contact/theatre/) (constants imported from `ContactTheatreConfig.js` in `AppManager.ts`).
- Do not reintroduce **parallel** contact stage ownership outside this pipeline.

---

## 6. Configuration and environment

- **[`config/setup.php`](../config/setup.php)** — defines `ROOT_PATH`, loads `.env` if present, sets error reporting, session, locale list, and includes `config/project.php` / `config/configuration.php` as applicable.
- **[`config/project.php`](../config/project.php)** — project-specific constants (e.g. admin directory name, upload bases). **`AdminDirectoryResolver`** uses this to detect admin requests in `src/autoload.php`.
- **[`config/helpers.php`](../config/helpers.php)** — view/render helpers; keep render paths stable for TS `data-page` expectations.

---

## 7. Change rules

- Before adding a token, search: `abstract/_colors.scss`, `abstract/_variables.scss`, `abstract/_headings.scss`, `base/_root.scss`.
- Reuse if meaning exists; add to shared layer if reusable; keep truly one-off values local (comment only if non-obvious).

### 7.2 PHP views

### 7.3 TypeScript / Three.js

- Page scene → `resource/ts/pages/<page>/scene`.
- Shared engine/runtime code stays out of page folders.
- New cross-page types → `resource/ts/types/*.types.ts`.

### 7.4 Routes and APIs

- New **JSON** endpoints → `Http\Response::json()` (or `response()` helper) with explicit status and shape; avoid mixing HTML and JSON handlers in the same closure without clear naming.
- **Works-related** list/detail/category behavior → extend [`api/works.php`](../api/works.php) and keep routes thin.

### 7.5 Admin

  - Component-local Sass aliases duplicating root tokens.

1	# CASE_STUDY
2	
3	Last updated: 2026-03-24
4	
5	## Goal
6	
7	Record the practical patterns behind high-end atmospheric backgrounds, cloud layers, reveal staging, lightweight visual runtimes, and responsive runtime architecture.
8	This document tracks what is worth borrowing into this project.
9	
10	## What Actually Creates Depth
11	
12	- Depth does not come from one strong plane.
13	- Depth comes from layered roles:
14	  - rear haze
15	  - mid body
16	  - front accent
17	- Each layer must differ in:
18	  - `z`
19	  - `scale`
20	  - `opacity`
21	  - motion speed
22	  - density
23	  - edge breakup
24	- Natural edges come from erosion and density breakup, not from a rectangular alpha fill.
25	- Camera-safe staging is geometry first, shader second.
26	- Big-agency look is usually 2D or 2.5D layered noise, not heavy volumetric raymarch.
27	
28	## Case References
29	
30	### Bruno Arizio Portfolio
31	Source:
32	https://tympanus.net/codrops/2019/12/18/case-study-portfolio-of-bruno-arizio/
33	
34	Useful takeaways:
35	- bend geometry separately from shader distortion

# CASE_STUDY

Last updated: 2026-03-24

## Goal

Record the practical patterns behind high-end atmospheric backgrounds, cloud layers, reveal staging, lightweight visual runtimes, and responsive runtime architecture.
This document tracks what is worth borrowing into this project.

## What Actually Creates Depth

- Depth does not come from one strong plane.
- Depth comes from layered roles:
  - rear haze
  - mid body
  - front accent
- Each layer must differ in:
  - `z`
  - `scale`
  - `opacity`
  - motion speed
  - density
  - edge breakup
- Natural edges come from erosion and density breakup, not from a rectangular alpha fill.
- Camera-safe staging is geometry first, shader second.
- Big-agency look is usually 2D or 2.5D layered noise, not heavy volumetric raymarch.

## Case References

### Bruno Arizio Portfolio
Source:
https://tympanus.net/codrops/2019/12/18/case-study-portfolio-of-bruno-arizio/

Useful takeaways:
- bend geometry separately from shader distortion
- normalize scroll values before feeding shaders
- keep author-facing controls small and meaningful

Applied here:
- `Background` owns curved geometry
- `CloudPlane` owns cloud material and breakup
- Theatre should author placement, not raw reactive math

### Stefan Vitasovic Portfolio 2025
Source:
https://tympanus.net/codrops/2025/03/05/case-study-stefan-vitasovic-portfolio-2025/

Useful takeaways:
- shared geometry and shared shader assets reduce cost
- multiple subtle layers feel deeper than one strong layer
- motion difference between layers matters more than raw opacity

Applied here:
- cloud planes share texture assets
- six cloud layers are better than one oversized overlay

### Ronin161 Portfolio 2024
Source:
https://tympanus.net/codrops/2024/02/20/case-study-ronin161s-portfolio-2024/

Useful takeaways:
- noisy erosion beats hard alpha edges
- shape quality matters before post-processing
- interaction should disturb local structure, not flatten the whole layer

Applied here:
- cloud edges should erode, not form a visible rectangle
- mouse effect should be gentle push plus light fade

### Stas Bondar 2025
Source:
https://tympanus.net/codrops/2025/03/25/stas-bondar-25-the-code-techniques-behind-a-next-level-portfolio/

Useful takeaways:
- orchestration layer and render layer must stay separate
- page-specific art direction can sit on top of shared runtime patterns
- motion, layout, and shader response should not live in one class

Applied here:
- `Background` and `CloudPlane` remain separate classes
- Theatre placement and runtime reaction stay split

### Three.js Responsive Design Manual
Source:
https://threejs.org/manual/en/responsive.html

Useful takeaways:
- CSS layout size and WebGL drawing-buffer size must be treated separately
- camera aspect and renderer size must be updated from one resize path
- device pixel ratio should be capped intentionally, not left fully uncapped

Applied here:
- `ResponsiveRuntime` becomes the single viewport and DPR authority
- `Engine.applyResponsiveSnapshot()` applies camera aspect and renderer DPR together
- object-level responsive logic should consume runtime snapshots instead of reading `window` directly

### Instrument Design System Pattern
Sources:
https://www.instrument.com/work/nike-digital-design-system
https://www.instrument.com/work/eames-institute
https://www.instrument.com/work/iru-launch

Useful takeaways:
- large teams do not let pages invent independent responsive rules
- shared component systems and one source of truth are required for consistency
- art direction can vary per page while core layout tokens stay centralized

Applied here:
- responsive behavior should be owned by one runtime service, not scattered across scene objects
- page scenes can still choose different offsets and scales, but they should resolve from shared tokens
- Three and DOM should consume the same breakpoint and scale vocabulary

### makemepulse Runtime Pattern
Sources:
https://www.makemepulse.com/news/nanogl--a-crafted-webgl2-microframework
https://www.makemepulse.com/case-study/unesco-virtual-museum-of-stolen-cultural-objects

Useful takeaways:
- responsive handling in WebGL projects is also a performance-budget problem
- mobile and compact screens often require different shader cost, texture cost, and DPR limits
- quality scaling belongs to runtime policy, not ad-hoc per component tweaks

Applied here:
- `PerformanceProfile` now resolves from a runtime environment snapshot
- DPR, quality tier, and reduced-motion policy should all come from one responsive source
- visual modules like `WorldMarquee` should only consume interpreted responsive values

## Current Project Decisions

### Background
- background is now a fullscreen render-target service
- per-sheet shader variants live behind one runtime API
- art direction still exists per sheet, but shader variants are intentionally shared where the runtime policy says they should be:
  - `intro` and `introAction` share the `introAction` variant
  - `why`, `services`, `works`, `worksDetail`, `worksFinal` currently resolve through the `services` variant family
  - `client`, `contact`, `footer` currently resolve through the `client` variant family
- sheet switching can use either:
  - generic background transition shader
  - section-specific foreground reveal object

### Clouds
- six layers
  - `rear haze A`
  - `rear haze B`
  - `mid body A`
  - `mid body B`
  - `front accent A`
  - `front accent B`
- Theatre owns transform authoring
- runtime owns live mouse field
- shared perlin/noise textures
- real-time `DataTexture` drives pointer interaction

### Foreground reveal
- `who` no longer depends on background-only handoff
- Earth reveal uses a dedicated foreground veil plane:
  - separate scene object
  - transparent shader
  - no depth write
  - camera-follow staging
- this matches the practical pattern where the target stays stable and the front layer performs the reveal

## New Case Pattern Added

### Earth reveal staging
Useful takeaway:
- when a hero object should emerge naturally, a foreground veil is often better than fading the object itself
- reveal should happen in spatial layers:
  - background stays stable
  - subject stays stable
  - front veil controls the cinematic handoff

Applied here:
- `story -> who` uses veil-only transition
- background transition is intentionally skipped on that handoff
- reveal opens from the center outward, matching the desired "curtain from the middle" feel

### Main page atmosphere handoff
Useful takeaway:
- a section handoff does not always need a hard variant jump
- keeping one shader family active while blending only the art-direction look can feel smoother

Applied here:
- `who` keeps the `who` background family active
- local scroll progress blends the background look toward the darker `services` atmosphere
- `why` and the later works-side sections currently switch through the `services` variant directly
- `contact` and `footer` currently stay within the `client` variant family while using their own look values

### Lightweight decorative canvases
Useful takeaway:
- not every visual card needs to enter the main Three.js engine
- small presentational motion can stay in local canvas runtimes when it does not need scene depth or theatre control

Applied here:
- who feature cards use local 2D canvas drawing for simple cube and particle decoration
- works scatter cards use their own dedicated Three runtime instead of entering the main scene engine path

### Responsive runtime as first-class app service
Useful takeaway:
- large interactive sites treat responsive logic as application state, not just CSS behavior
- breakpoint, DPR, motion preference, device tier, and world-scale tokens should be computed once
- the resize path should distribute one normalized snapshot to renderers, UI, and scene objects

Applied here:
- `ResponsiveRuntime` now owns:
  - breakpoint
  - viewport
  - reduced-motion state
  - hover/pointer capability
  - DPR cap
  - performance tier
  - shared scale tokens
- `ResizeSetup` refreshes the responsive snapshot first, then updates engine viewport
- `Engine` no longer acts as the primary responsive decision-maker; it consumes snapshot output
- `WorldMarquee` uses shared responsive number resolution rather than hardcoded desktop-only sizing

### Responsive marquee lesson
Useful takeaway:
- repeated text systems should not encode spacing rules partly in the source string and partly in runtime gaps
- repeat boundary, separator, font scaling, and texture ratio must be owned by one module

Applied here:
- marquee text is trimmed of trailing separators before repetition
- `repeatSeparator` owns loop boundary spacing
- `ResponsiveValue` resolves fluid values for font size, height, and canvas sizing
- texture aspect and plane aspect are kept aligned to avoid compressed typography

## Big-Agency Pattern To Keep

1. Geometry provides safety.
2. Shader provides texture and behavior.
3. Runtime provides reaction.
4. Theatre provides placement and cinematic timing.
5. Foreground reveal layers handle special handoffs better than forcing them into the background system.
6. Responsive rules should be centralized as runtime state, not re-invented per scene object.

If one layer owns all four, maintenance quality drops fast.

## Next Quality Moves

- give each cloud layer its own time multiplier
- give each cloud layer its own density bias
- give each cloud layer its own erosion strength
- keep pointer response subtle and local
- avoid solving weak depth with only bloom
- tune `story -> who` veil timing against actual theatre keyframes
- keep generic background transition out of special reveal moments
- split decorative card canvas presets by card meaning if the section becomes permanent
- move remaining `DEFAULT_THREE` consumers toward `ResponsiveRuntime` snapshots
- expose more shared world tokens for camera offsets, object scale, and typography
- let UI and Three read the same responsive CSS variables and runtime snapshot

## Anti-Patterns

- one giant opaque cloud plane
- hard rectangular alpha reinforcement
- static mouse mask image pretending to be live interaction
- background logic mixed into cloud logic
- Theatre directly owning low-level reactive uniforms
- moving decorative card canvases into the main scene engine without a real depth or timing need
- scene objects reading raw `window.innerWidth` as their primary responsive source
- mixing repeat separator logic into both content strings and runtime gap math
- treating responsive logic as resize-event plumbing only

## Summary

The strongest direction for this project is:
- one stable background service
- independent sheet variants behind that service
- multiple semantic cloud layers
- foreground reveal objects for scene-specific handoffs
- Theatre-driven staging
- runtime-driven interaction
- lightweight local canvas decoration for non-scene UI surfaces
- one responsive runtime that distributes breakpoint, DPR, quality, and scale policy across the app

That is the closest practical path to an awards-style cinematic result without turning the codebase into a shader dump.
